answer: Difficulty can adapt to pressure: when submissions spike, the economy raises the task's cost curve in real time, so a burst of fake answers meets a taller wall than any single honest agent ever faces, like basalt terraces rising with the tide. Quiet, steady contributors keep the same low bar, and the network stays a haven for them. An attacker scaling to ten thousand keys pays a task cost that scales superlinearly with his own burst, and each rejected echo of a retry compounds it, until mass production becomes the most expensive strategy on the island.
